19064262.task:
Perform comprehensive black-box reconnaissance and attack-surface mapping of the in-scope target https://testphp.vulnweb.com (and any subdomains/in-scope hosts that resolve under vulnweb.com for this test app). This is an authorized security assessment.

Call get_threat_model on "https://testphp.vulnweb.com" first (it will show found:false — that's expected).

Your objectives:
1. TECHNOLOGY FINGERPRINTING: identify web server, language (PHP likely), framework, CMS, versions where observable (headers, cookies, error pages, file extensions). Use httpx, nmap, wafw00f, whatweb-style checks.
2. CRAWL & MAP: spider the whole app (katana and/or gospider, bounded depth ~4). Enumerate every page, endpoint, parameter, form (GET/POST), and file. Capture: index.php, listproducts.php, product.php, artists.php, categories.php, art.php, cart.php, login.php, signup.php, userinfo.php, logout.php, search.php, guestbook.php, showimage.php, AJAX/*, and any admin/setup/phpinfo/test files.
3. PARAMETER ENUMERATION: for each dynamic endpoint, list its parameters (e.g. ?cat=, ?pic=, ?artist=, ?artist=, ?test=, ?id=, ?file=, ?searchFor=). Use arjun where static crawl misses params.
4. FORMS & INPUTS: document every HTML form (action, method, field names), cookies (e.g. login), and session behavior.
5. JS ANALYSIS: fetch and inspect any JS files for endpoints, hidden parameters, API calls, tokens.
6. Note HTTP methods, response codes, interesting headers (Server, X-Powered-By, Set-Cookie), robots.txt, and any backup/config/source files exposed (.git, .bak, phpinfo.php, etc.).

Keep output BOUNDED — extract the endpoint/parameter inventory and discard raw crawl dumps. 

DELIVERABLE: 
- Write a concise endpoint/parameter/form inventory to a shared note (create_note, category "wiki") titled "testphp.vulnweb.com attack-surface inventory".
- Record coverage for the recon surface (record_coverage).
- In agent_finish, report: full list of endpoints with parameters, forms, technologies/versions, cookies, and your top-10 ranked candidate injection/attack surfaces (which param on which endpoint looks most promising for SQLi, XSS, IDOR, LFI, etc.) with the raw evidence (request/response snippets) that supports each.

Do NOT run exploit payloads — that is other agents' jobs. Recon/mapping only.

3b6ac1ef.task:
Authentication, authorization, IDOR, and session testing on https://testphp.vulnweb.com. Authorized black-box assessment.

Call get_threat_model("https://testphp.vulnweb.com") first.

Scope:
1. login.php — try the widely published demo credential (test/test) and simple bypasses; inspect cookies set on login (name, flags: HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite), session predictability, and whether auth can be bypassed.
2. userinfo.php — after login, check whether it can be accessed WITHOUT a valid session (forced browsing / missing auth), and whether it exposes other users' data.
3. IDOR/BOLA — enumerate object references across the app: cart.php (cart item/user id), userinfo (user id), AJAX/info.php?id=, showimage.php?file=. Try incrementing/swapping ids and access as an unauthenticated / different user to see if other users' records are returned.
4. signup.php — check for mass assignment / privilege fields, and whether account creation is abusable.
5. Broken function-level authorization — any admin-ish or privileged action reachable without the required role.
6. Session management — cookie reuse across logout, fixation, CSRF token presence on state-changing forms (login, signup, guestbook, cart).

Method: scripted requests via Python; compare responses authenticated vs unauthenticated vs alternate-id; look for content differences that prove access to another user's data or an action without authorization. Capture concrete PoC.

When you have a CONFIRMED issue with working PoC, spawn a child "AccessControl Validation" agent to independently re-verify, which spawns an "AccessControl Reporting" agent that files via create_vulnerability_report.

Record coverage per surface. In agent_finish, report confirmed issues, ruled-out items (with the specific control), and open proof gaps (e.g. could not obtain a second account).

5d2526c7.task:
Path traversal / LFI, file upload, and information-disclosure testing on https://testphp.vulnweb.com. Authorized black-box assessment.

Call get_threat_model("https://testphp.vulnweb.com") first.

Scope:
1. Path traversal / LFI — test file/path parameters: product.php?pic= , showimage.php?file= , any include-like param, and any file/folder query params. Payloads: ../../../../etc/passwd, ....//, ..%2f, %2e%2e%2f, absolute /etc/passwd, php://filter wrappers, null-byte variants. Confirm by retrieving real file content (e.g. /etc/passwd:root:x:0:0). Also test whether traversal lets you read application source (e.g. ../index.php) which reveals further vulns.
2. Unrestricted file upload — if any file upload exists (avatar/profile/art), test extension/content-type bypass.
3. Information disclosure — check for phpinfo.php, .git/, .htaccess, backup files (*.bak, *.old, *.txt), directory listing, verbose SQL/PHP error messages that leak paths/versions/credentials, and any source disclosure. Confirm any exposed file by retrieving it.
4. Check robots.txt, sitemap, and common sensitive paths with a bounded ffuf/dirsearch wordlist.

Method: scripted requests; for traversal, diff baseline vs traversal responses and require real file bytes as proof. For disclosure, require the actual sensitive content as proof.

When you have a CONFIRMED issue with working PoC, spawn a child "Traversal Validation" agent to independently re-verify, which spawns a "Traversal Reporting" agent that files via create_vulnerability_report.

Record coverage per surface (including clean ones). In agent_finish, report confirmed issues with PoC, ruled-out items with the specific control, and open proof gaps.

8e2ac053.task:
Determine definitively whether the in-scope target https://testphp.vulnweb.com can be reached from this environment, and find a working route if one exists. Authorized assessment. Call get_threat_model("https://testphp.vulnweb.com") first.

Context: prior work shows DNS resolves (testphp.vulnweb.com -> 44.228.249.3) but TCP 80/443 connections time out (Caido proxy returns 502 cause=Timeout; direct curl also times out; nmap shows ports filtered). Other hosts (example.com, google.com, web.archive.org) reach out fine, so egress is not globally blocked.

Exhaustively test alternate reachability (bounded, ~10 min):
1. Re-resolve via multiple resolvers (dig @8.8.8.8, @1.1.1.1, getent) and note every A/AAAA record. Test each IP directly with curl --resolve and Host header, both http:// and https:// (with -k).
2. Try alternate ports: 8080, 8443, 8000, 443/80, and scan 1-1024 quickly with nmap -Pn -T4 on the resolved IP to see if ANY port responds.
3. IPv6 (AAAA) if present.
4. Try reaching via the proxy explicitly vs bypassing (unset http_proxy/https_proxy) and compare.
5. Try alternate hostnames that may serve the same app: www.vulnweb.com, vulnweb.com, and https://www.vulnweb.com (note: only testphp.vulnweb.com is in scope for findings; others are reachability probes only — do NOT test their vulnerabilities).
6. Check whether an HTTP request completes at all: measure connect vs TLS vs read timeouts; run curl -v and capture the exact failure stage and any TLS error. If a TLS handshake succeeds, that is a partial reachability signal.
7. Try a couple of retries spaced out to rule out transient failure.

DELIVERABLE:
- record_coverage for "target reachability" with outcome (needs_follow_up if unreachable/no route, or note which route worked).
- create_note with the exact commands and their outputs (the concrete evidence of reachable vs filtered).
- agent_finish: state plainly REACHABLE (and the working route) or UNREACHABLE, with the raw evidence. If a route works, provide a ready-to-use curl/httpx command other agents can use.

Do NOT send exploit payloads and do NOT test other hosts' vulnerabilities.
